title: The last push to the Volga
pull: The last push to the Volga

facts.text: On 8 November 1942, Hitler told Nazi Party veterans in Munich that Stalingrad was all but taken.
On 11 November 1942, the German Sixth Army opened Operation Hubertus, its last offensive to take Stalingrad before the Soviet counteroffensive, with a heavy barrage before dawn.
Several pioneer (assault engineer) battalions were flown into Stalingrad for the attack.
The main objective was the Volga shoreline just east of the Barrikady gun factory.
The Germans reached the Volga on a front of about 600 yards near the Red October steel works.
They cut off Lyudnikov's 138th Rifle Division against the river in a pocket about 400 by 700 meters. The Volga had begun to freeze, making supply across it hard.
The 62nd Army held, and the attack faded. On 19 November the Red Army opened Operation Uranus.

declassified.fact: The cut off Soviet pocket became known as Lyudnikov's Island. It was not reunited with the rest of the 62nd Army until the last day of 1942.

body:
Hitler had told Germany that Stalingrad was all but taken. Three days later, the men of the Sixth Army were sent to finish the job.

11 November 1942. Operation Hubertus opened before dawn with a heavy barrage. Assault engineer battalions, flown in for the attack, pushed toward the Volga beside the ruined Barrikady gun factory and reached the river on a front of about 600 yards.

They cut off a Soviet division against the water in a strip about 400 by 700 meters. The river was starting to freeze, and supplies could barely get across.

The pocket held. Eight days later the Red Army's counteroffensive began, and the attackers became the trapped.
